cards.name: 1 x 2 (2-up)
cards.summary: Print imposition layout (a .cly file): a 1 x 2 grid, 2 pages up on each sheet; its file numbers the 2 cells 1 to 2. Not visual, so there is no look of its own. The name's two numbers match the first two grid values in the file; reading them as columns then rows fits 'Readers Spread' but was not confirmed.
use_for: two-up proofs and flyers on one sheet
A5 pieces gang-run on an A4 sheet
saving paper on short runs
avoid: Only the grid and page numbers of the file were read (margins and gutters were not decoded) and no cell is turned: the rest of this card is built from the name and standard print terms; check the layout in Print Preview before sending a job.
Booklets or any job where pages must be in reading order: an n-up grid does not fold; use one of the 8-up saddle-stitch or perfect-bound layouts.
Setting the sheet size: the layout only arranges pages; set the paper size and printer in the print dialog.
cards.applies_to: a print job, not an object: it tells the print engine how to arrange the document's pages on each press sheet; it works on the open document at print time and changes no object
cards.how_to_apply: File > Print (Ctrl+P, Automation.InvokeItem("e3f5366a-09aa-4824-96b2-730b8926a3c6")) > Layout tab, or File > Print Preview (Automation.InvokeItem("51771ba9-7ada-4863-92f0-37148c401066")) with its Imposition Layout tool; pick '1 x 2 (2-up)' in the imposition layout list (the usual route; the harvest read the layout file only and did not open either dialog, so the exact list is unconfirmed). It is the file Custom Data/Layouts/1 x 2 (2-up).cly in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: no call that loads an imposition layout was found in the harvest. Read from the file as 32-bit values: the grid (1, 2) and 2 cells stored as (page, rotation) pairs, pages 1 to 2, none turned; margins and gutters were not decoded.

verified.note: No thumbnail (print imposition layout, not visual); the .cly read as 32-bit values confirms the (1, 2) grid and cells 1 to 2 the card states.

review.changes: how_to_apply: said the page order was not decoded (contradicting the summary); now gives what the file holds; avoid: rotations removed from the undecoded list (all cells are unturned)

cards.name: 8-up Perfect Bound - Sheetwise
cards.id: Custom Data/Layouts/8-up Perfect Bound - Sheetwise.cly#8-up Perfect Bound - Sheetwise
cards.summary: Print imposition layout (a .cly file) for an 8-up booklet signature, intended for perfect binding (folded sections gathered and glued at a squared spine), using the Sheetwise method (front and back sides use two separate plates, with the sheet turned over between passes). Not visual, so there is no look of its own; the page order is built into the layout: its file holds a 4 x 2 grid with page positions 1 to 16 (8 on each side of the sheet), and the first four cells of each side are stored turned 180 degrees (head-to-head placement).
use_for: glued-spine catalogues, manuals and books printed on a press
sixteen-page signatures with both sides imposed
commercial book printing
avoid: Only the grid and page numbers of the file were read (margins and gutters were not decoded): the rest of this card is built from the name and standard print terms; check the layout in Print Preview before sending a job.
Expecting different page orders from the Perfect Bound and Saddle-Stitch versions of the same method: their files hold identical page positions and differ only by a binding flag value.
Single-page jobs: the layout assumes a multi-page document with a page count that fits the 8-up signature (multiples of the sheet's page count), so pad the document with blank pages if needed.
Choosing the wrong turn: Sheetwise, Work & Turn and Work & Tumble need different press set-ups; ask the printer which one they run.
cards.applies_to: a print job, not an object: it tells the print engine how to arrange the document's pages on each press sheet; it works on the open document at print time and changes no object
cards.how_to_apply: File > Print (Ctrl+P, Automation.InvokeItem("e3f5366a-09aa-4824-96b2-730b8926a3c6")) > Layout tab, or File > Print Preview (Automation.InvokeItem("51771ba9-7ada-4863-92f0-37148c401066")) with its Imposition Layout tool; pick '8-up Perfect Bound - Sheetwise' in the imposition layout list (the usual route; the harvest read the layout file only and did not open either dialog, so the exact list is unconfirmed). It is the file Custom Data/Layouts/8-up Perfect Bound - Sheetwise.cly in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: no call that loads an imposition layout was found in the harvest. Read from the file as 32-bit values: a 4 x 2 grid, cell pages in file order side 1: 9* 8* 5* 12* 16 1 4 13, side 2: 11* 6* 7* 10* 14 3 2 15; * marks a cell stored with rotation 180000000 (180 degrees in CorelDRAW's millionths-of-a-degree angle unit, the unit of the 45000000 screen angle in FountainFills.cdss), so the first four cells of each side are turned head to head with the other four. Margins and gutters were not decoded.

verified.note: No thumbnail (not visual); the .cly confirms the 4 x 2 grid, pages 1 to 16 on two sides, identical Perfect Bound / Saddle-Stitch page order differing in one flag, and the 180-degree cells.

review.changes: summary: the 180-degree turn of the first four cells of each side confirmed (angle unit), no longer "not confirmed"; how_to_apply: page order read from the file added (it said page order was not decoded); avoid: rotations removed from the undecoded list

cards.id: Custom Data/Layouts/8-up Saddle-Stitch - Sheetwise.cly#8-up Saddle-Stitch - Sheetwise
cards.summary: Print imposition layout (a .cly file) for an 8-up booklet signature, intended for saddle-stitch binding (sheets nested, folded and stapled through the spine fold), using the Sheetwise method (front and back sides use two separate plates, with the sheet turned over between passes). Not visual, so there is no look of its own; the page order is built into the layout: its file holds a 4 x 2 grid with page positions 1 to 16 (8 on each side of the sheet), and the first four cells of each side are stored turned 180 degrees (head-to-head placement).
use_for: stapled booklets, programmes and magazines printed on a press
sixteen-page signatures with both sides imposed
commercial booklet printing
avoid: Only the grid and page numbers of the file were read (margins and gutters were not decoded): the rest of this card is built from the name and standard print terms; check the layout in Print Preview before sending a job.
Expecting different page orders from the Perfect Bound and Saddle-Stitch versions of the same method: their files hold identical page positions and differ only by a binding flag value.
Single-page jobs: the layout assumes a multi-page document with a page count that fits the 8-up signature (multiples of the sheet's page count), so pad the document with blank pages if needed.
Choosing the wrong turn: Sheetwise, Work & Turn and Work & Tumble need different press set-ups; ask the printer which one they run.
cards.applies_to: a print job, not an object: it tells the print engine how to arrange the document's pages on each press sheet; it works on the open document at print time and changes no object
cards.how_to_apply: File > Print (Ctrl+P, Automation.InvokeItem("e3f5366a-09aa-4824-96b2-730b8926a3c6")) > Layout tab, or File > Print Preview (Automation.InvokeItem("51771ba9-7ada-4863-92f0-37148c401066")) with its Imposition Layout tool; pick '8-up Saddle-Stitch - Sheetwise' in the imposition layout list (the usual route; the harvest read the layout file only and did not open either dialog, so the exact list is unconfirmed). It is the file Custom Data/Layouts/8-up Saddle-Stitch - Sheetwise.cly in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: no call that loads an imposition layout was found in the harvest. Read from the file as 32-bit values: a 4 x 2 grid, cell pages in file order side 1: 9* 8* 5* 12* 16 1 4 13, side 2: 11* 6* 7* 10* 14 3 2 15; * marks a cell stored with rotation 180000000 (180 degrees in CorelDRAW's millionths-of-a-degree angle unit, the unit of the 45000000 screen angle in FountainFills.cdss), so the first four cells of each side are turned head to head with the other four. Margins and gutters were not decoded.

verified.note: No thumbnail (not visual); the .cly confirms the 4 x 2 grid, pages 1 to 16 on two sides, identical Perfect Bound / Saddle-Stitch page order differing in one flag, and the 180-degree cells.

review.changes: summary: the 180-degree turn of the first four cells of each side confirmed (angle unit), no longer "not confirmed"; how_to_apply: page order read from the file added (it said page order was not decoded); avoid: rotations removed from the undecoded list

cards.name: Readers Spread
cards.summary: Print imposition layout (a .cly file) named 'Readers Spread': by its name it lays pages out as two-page spreads in reading order, the way a reader sees an open book, rather than in printer's order. Its file holds the same two-cell grid as '2 x 1 (2-up)', differing by one flag value (what that flag switches was not confirmed). Not visual, so there is no look of its own.
use_for: proof copies of a book or booklet to read in page order
checking spreads before final imposition
office printouts of facing pages
avoid: Only the grid and page numbers of the file were read (margins and gutters were not decoded) and no cell is turned: the rest of this card is built from the name and standard print terms; check the layout in Print Preview before sending a job.
Final press work: reader's spreads are not folded-signature order, so a press cannot fold and bind them; use an 8-up saddle-stitch or perfect-bound layout.
cards.applies_to: a print job, not an object: it tells the print engine how to arrange the document's pages on each press sheet; it works on the open document at print time and changes no object
cards.how_to_apply: File > Print (Ctrl+P, Automation.InvokeItem("e3f5366a-09aa-4824-96b2-730b8926a3c6")) > Layout tab, or File > Print Preview (Automation.InvokeItem("51771ba9-7ada-4863-92f0-37148c401066")) with its Imposition Layout tool; pick 'Readers Spread' in the imposition layout list (the usual route; the harvest read the layout file only and did not open either dialog, so the exact list is unconfirmed). It is the file Custom Data/Layouts/Readers Spread.cly in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: no call that loads an imposition layout was found in the harvest. Read from the file as 32-bit values: the grid (2, 1) and 2 cells stored as (page, rotation) pairs, pages 1 to 2, none turned; margins and gutters were not decoded.

verified.note: No thumbnail (not visual); the .cly confirms the 2 x 1 grid of 2 x 1 (2-up) with one flag value different (3 vs 1), as the card states.

review.changes: how_to_apply: said the page order was not decoded (contradicting the summary); now gives what the file holds; avoid: rotations removed from the undecoded list (all cells are unturned)

cards.name: InnerShadow1
cards.summary: Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows a pale-yellow square (#FFFFCC) with an even, soft olive-grey shadow (#979778) just inside all four edges: no offset, a feathered band about a sixth of the square's width, strong at the outer edge and fading toward the middle. Applied to your own object it carries the shadow settings, not the pale-yellow square.
use_for: soft inset or 'pressed-in' panels, cards and input fields
a gentle vignette inside a badge or button
pillow-like depth on flat shapes
avoid: A directional light: the shadow is even all round, so it does not say where the light comes from; use one of the offset ones (InnerShadow3 to InnerShadow6).
Very thin shapes: the band is about a sixth of the object's width and can fill a narrow object.
cards.applies_to: one vector object selected with the Inner Shadow tool: it adds a live inner shadow (shading just inside the object's edge); the object stays editable and the shadow can be cleared. The preview's pale-yellow square is not part of the preset
cards.how_to_apply: Toolbox > Shadow > Inner Shadow tool (Automation.InvokeItem("08f5977a-dd28-b8b1-4fe0-767c7eb7147e")): select the object, then pick 'InnerShadow1' in the Preset list on the property bar (the usual route; the harvest read the .pst file but did not walk the property bar, so the exact list is unconfirmed). It is the file Draw/Presets/Shadow/InnerShadow1.pst in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: the harvest records no call that applies a .pst preset (its 111-byte parameter block is undocumented). Scripted substitute: Shape.CreateInnerShadow(Opacity, Feather, OffsetX, OffsetY, Color, FeatherType, FeatherEdge, MergeMode, Depth) set to match the preview (OffsetX = 0, OffsetY = 0, as the .pst parameter block stores them; a wide soft Feather, Opacity high); approximate, not tested by the harvest.

verified.note: Shipped preview: pale-yellow #FFFFCC square, even olive-grey #979778 band about 50 px of 296 (a sixth) on all four sides, no offset (file offset 0, 0), as described.

review.changes: how_to_apply: zero offset confirmed from the .pst parameter block
